after.description: Return events strictly after this cursor value

limit.description: Maximum number of events per page

response.feed_sha256: string (64-char hex SHA-256 digest of feed facts)

create_remote_session.idempotency: Enforced by operation_id. Duplicate operation_id returns existing session.

stop_remote_session.idempotency: Idempotent by immutable session_id. Concurrent calls are serialized by a database row lock. A retry after a lost 200 response returns the same durable closed session without repeating resource teardown or lifecycle events.

request_body.tenant_id: integer or null; optional expected identity guard
request_body.sn: string or null; optional expected identity guard
request_body.timeout_sec: number or null; graceful console stop timeout in range 0..60 seconds

success.meaning: The response body is the committed terminal session record and status is closed (or failed if the session was already terminal). For a normal stop, 200 confirms durable closed and completed resource teardown.
success.reconciliation: GET /api/internal/v1/remote-sessions/{session_id}; consumers must reconcile by the same session_id and must not infer closure from stream/media state alone.

404.meaning: The exact session_id is unknown. No other session is selected or stopped.

409.meaning: Provided tenant_id and/or sn does not match the durable session. No lifecycle transition or teardown is performed.

503.meaning: The session is durably stopping because resource teardown failed. retryable=true; repeat stop for the same session_id or reconcile until terminal.

concurrency.stop_vs_stop: Calls for the same session_id join through row-level serialization; only one teardown and one stop_requested/closed event pair is produced.
concurrency.stop_vs_create: stopping remains a blocking state for the same SN. Create returns the existing session_busy 409 until stop is durably closed.
concurrency.late_old_stop: A stop for an already closed old session_id is a no-op on that record and never tears down a newer session or its owned lease.

invariants: Cursor is strictly monotonically increasing (BigInteger autoincrement sequence)
Event feed is append-only and deterministic in cursor ASC order
Duplicate deliveries by event_id or (operation_id + event_type) are idempotently deduped
A normal stop 200 response means the session is durably closed; stopping is never reported as successful closure
requested, starting, active, and stopping all block creation of another session for the same SN
Stop targets only the explicit session_id and optional tenant_id/SN guards; no latest-session lookup is used
A lease owned by another session_id is never revoked by a late stop
occurred_at and created_at timestamps are strictly UTC ISO 8601
Payloads are validated against commercial field injection (no financial data in IoT feed)
Agent MQTT protocol remains completely unchanged and binary backward-compatible
